reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes Bitcoin participation through a premium webinar while presenting Bitcoin as economically beneficial, comparing it to gold, claiming that mining is automatically credited to her account, and suggesting its price can rise. She presents these investment and mining claims as personal benefits and ends by urging viewers to follow the premium webinar, with a contact number and external link provided for participation.

citations.quote: What I found out during this training was that Bitcoin is an anti-inflation currency.
When I start to buy Bitcoin, the price was around 650,000 IDR Now, the price is almost 60,000 IDR
the process of mining is automatically automatically uploaded to my account
In my opinion, let's follow this premium online webinar
For more information, contact SAFIRA AMALIA at [PHONE] or visit http://bit.ly/BCN_INDO.

opening.argument: The speaker presents her remarks as personal experience and opinion, not as a guaranteed investment outcome. She identifies herself as an alumna who benefited from the webinar and explicitly qualifies the recommendation with “In my opinion.” Her statements therefore read as subjective investment commentary: she explains what she learned, describes her own confidence, and offers a view about Bitcoin's future rather than promising that every viewer will profit. The supplied material contains no explicit guarantee, fixed-return promise, or assurance that viewers cannot lose money. A persuasive opinion about an asset's potential is not by itself proof of deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: I am also an alumni at this Bitcoin Online Premium Webinar I have gained a lot of benefits
As such I was excited to invest and also feeling that I was confident in investing in this coin
In my opinion, let's follow this premium online webinar

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution turns optimistic commentary into a guarantee. Calling Bitcoin “anti-inflation,” comparing it to gold, and describing personal confidence are evaluative statements, but none says a viewer will receive a specified return or cannot lose money. The mining statement is also reported as the speaker's own experience, not independently presented proof of a guaranteed payout. Finally, the contact details show a way to obtain information, not that deception or a compulsory deposit occurred.

citations.quote: Bitcoin is an anti-inflation currency
even like gold coin has same quality quality with the gold coin
For more information, contact SAFIRA AMALIA at [PHONE] or visit http://bit.ly/BCN_INDO.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The first-person framing does not neutralize the economic claims. The speaker says the webinar taught her “how is the profit” and “how to make profit,” then links buying Bitcoin to a dramatic price increase and says mining is automatically credited to her account. Her opinion is immediately followed by an invitation to join the premium webinar, while the description supplies a contact route and link. That combination is promotional investment inducement even without a literal fixed-return promise.

citations.quote: I learned about Bitcoin How is the profit And how to use it, how to make profit
When I start to buy Bitcoin, the price was around 650,000 IDR Now, the price is almost 60,000 IDR
the process of mining is automatically automatically uploaded to my account
In my opinion, let's follow this premium online webinar

opening.argument: The video's central activity is explaining a technology and recounting what an attendee learned in a Bitcoin webinar. The speaker discusses what Bitcoin is, how profit is understood, how to use it, and how mining works. That is consistent with educational or operational commentary, particularly because she identifies herself as an alumna and describes the process she says she experienced. The video does not show a transaction screen, a payment instruction, a registration procedure, or a demonstrated transfer of funds. An invitation to learn through a premium webinar can be ordinary educational promotion; the supplied evidence does not establish that the presentation's primary purpose is a scam rather than explaining a technology and a personal experience.

citations.quote: I learned about Bitcoin How is the profit And how to use it, how to make profit, and how to use it.
Praise to god, I've been practicing mining bitcoin for some time
the process of mining is automatically automatically uploaded to my account
I am also an alumni at this Bitcoin Online Premium Webinar

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution labels the educational subject matter as solicitation without showing a payment process. Its quoted invitation is an invitation to follow a webinar, not an instruction to transfer money or a claim that enrollment guarantees returns. The speaker's statements about Bitcoin's characteristics and mining can be understood as the content of the lesson she is recounting. The description's phrase “For more information” likewise leaves the destination and purpose unspecified.

citations.quote: In my opinion, let's follow this premium online webinar
For more information, contact SAFIRA AMALIA at [PHONE] or visit http://bit.ly/BCN_INDO.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not merely neutral instruction. The speaker says she gained benefits, became confident investing, describes Bitcoin as economically protective, reports automated mining credit, and concludes by urging viewers toward the premium webinar. Those are benefits and participation claims used to motivate the audience. The absence of a visible checkout screen does not erase the spoken promotion or the supplied contact link.

citations.quote: I have gained a lot of benefits
Bitcoin is very good to your health and good for your economy
the process of mining is automatically automatically uploaded to my account
let's follow this premium online webinar

opening.argument: At most, the material shows promotion of an ordinary paid information service and discussion of purchasing an asset. The description offers contact information and a link “for more information,” while the speaker invites viewers to follow a premium webinar. That is compatible with ordinary service referral or educational commerce. Crucially, the supplied record does not show a requested deposit, a guaranteed return, a downline or recruitment scheme, a credential request, or a required payment amount. It also does not establish who operates the link or what happens after contact. Those missing mechanisms matter: enthusiasm and an asset-price discussion alone do not establish deceptive commerce.

citations.quote: For more information, contact SAFIRA AMALIA at [PHONE] or visit http://bit.ly/BCN_INDO.
In my opinion, let's follow this premium online webinar
When I start to buy Bitcoin, the price was around 650,000 IDR Now, the price is almost 60,000 IDR

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers a scam mechanism from an information contact and favorable claims, but the record does not show a deposit demand, account credentials, mandatory purchase, or promised commission. The phrase “premium online webinar” identifies a service that may be paid, yet it does not specify its price or falsely guarantee an outcome. Even the link is presented only as a source of more information, so its destination and operation cannot be assumed.

citations.quote: For more information, contact SAFIRA AMALIA at [PHONE] or visit http://bit.ly/BCN_INDO.
In my opinion, let's follow this premium online webinar

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam need not display a checkout screen when the persuasive mechanism is the promised economic benefit of participation. The speaker says she learned how to make profit, calls Bitcoin beneficial to the economy, reports mining crediting automatically, and highlights a dramatic price increase. She then directs viewers to a premium webinar, with a phone number and link supplied for follow-up. That is more than a neutral price listing or ordinary service advertisement.
